newsitem.title: DENMARK: Warring bikers rock Danish town with bomb blast.
newsitem.headline: Warring bikers rock Danish town with bomb blast.

text.p: A car bomb exploded outside a Hell's Angels clubhouse in a sleepy seaside Danish town on Thursday, causing extensive damage but no injuries, police said.
It was the second car bomb in eight days, and the latest blow in a Nordic war between the Hell's Angels motorcycle gang and the rival Bandidos which has killed six people in two years.
The bomb, in the town of Roskilde, was planted in the engine compartment of a stolen Opel Kadett parked at the back of the clubhouse in a densely populated residential district .

Witnesses said the early morning blast hurled the car's engine 10 metres (yards) through the air and shunted the blazing vehicle along the ground, Danish radio and the national news agency Ritzau reported.

The bomb shattered windows in a 150-metre radius, blew out the front of a post office building and hurled the car's gear box into the wall of an apartment building near a window beneath which an elderly couple were sleeping.
Police did not say how much explosive the bomb contained.
It was not immediately clear if anyone was inside the clubhouse, whose roof was damaged in the blast.

A territorial dispute between the Hells' Angels and the Bandidos -- both Nordic offshoots of U.S. motorcycle clans -- flared in 1994 when a lone Hell's Angel member was murdered in Helsingborg in Sweden.
The most recent killing was in July when a Danish member of the Bandidos gang was shot dead in Norway, hit several times outside an abandoned clubhouse near the city of Drammen.
Residents of Roskilde, who had opposed the Hell's Angels recent move into the town 30 km (19 miles) southeast of Copenhagen, complained bitterly to police and reporters.
"Ever since the (Hell's Angels) sign went up, we have been afraid that this would happen," a woman who gave her name as Birthe told the news agency.
Last week, a car bomb apparently aimed at a member of a Hell's Angels-allied bike gang exploded in a car park in the Danish city of Aalborg. No one was hurt.
Police in southern Sweden arrested 12 Hell's Angels members in a series of raids on Tuesday and questioned them on suspicion of conspiracy to murder.
